newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber softens on Thai spillover.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber softens on Thai spillover.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices generally softened in early trading on Wednesday as the market kept an eye on the baht, traders said.
Thailand sent shock waves through Asian currency markets by floating the battered baht, a move which analysts said was a de facto devaluation.
"The market is keeping an eye on the developments in the Thai currency crisis, which I think will lead to a devaluation," said one trader.
"It will mean that Thailand will be selling rubber and that prices would be cheaper. Indonesia will have to take action by also selling cheaper rubber before it is too late," he said.
"Buyers will take a wait-and-see attitude while waiting for rubber prices to decline further. In general, I tend to think that we are entering a gloomy period again," he added.
Traders said a deal was done overnight at 44.00 U.S. cents/lb for September shipment fob Palembang, at 43.75 fob Padang and at 44.50 fob Jambi for October shipment.
Offer prices were quoted at 44.00 fob Surabaya for September shipment and at 43.50 fob Palembang, traders said.
They said traders in Medan insisted on selling rubber at 45.00.
"Those traders cannot enter the market because of the high offer prices. In a way, this makes sense because raw material is still tight there," said one trader.
"I think the rest of the day will be dominated by Thailand," he said.
